facts.fact: A conversion window is typically 30 days, starting immediately after a user views or clicks on an ad.
facts.quote: A conversion window is typically 30 days, and the window starts immediately after a user views or clicks on an ad.

facts.fact: In StackAdapt's DSP, the view-through and click-through conversion window defaults to 30 days.
facts.quote: In a DSP, the view-through (and click-through) window defaults to 30 days.

facts.fact: According to StackAdapt, the longer the conversion window is, the more conversions advertisers typically see.
facts.quote: The longer the conversion window is, the more conversions you’ll typically see.

facts.fact: A view-through conversion occurs when a user is served an ad for the first time, does not click it, and converts at a later time within the VTC window.
facts.quote: a view-through conversion happens when someone is served with an ad for the first time—their first impression—doesn’t click on it, but converts at a later time.

facts.fact: A click-through conversion occurs when a user clicks an ad and later converts as a direct result of clicking that ad, with the clock starting at the click.
facts.quote: By definition, a click-through conversion is when a user clicks an ad and later converts as a direct result of clicking that ad.

facts.fact: Conversions can be any valuable action, such as booking a test drive via a 300×600 banner click or downloading an eBook after a native ad.
facts.quote: someone clicking through on your 300×600 banner to book a test drive at your dealership, someone downloading an eBook after being served with a native ad
